generator.program.note: The lineage's own program (growth plan G2.3a), on the broadleaf base: it gives the values its species leave unset, which the broadleaf program gave as defaults until then.

traits.note: Watson and Dallwitz's description of the family (the DELTA distribution's own page for it, read 2026-10-15): flowers regular, (3-)4-6(-20)-merous; calyx (3-)4-5(-16), commonly fleshy or leathery, persistent; petals free, often shorter than the sepals; androecium 8-40, usually twice the petals (diplostemonous); gynoecium superior to inferior, the ovary 1-locular or 2-5(-20)-locular; a free hypanthium present or absent, so none is stated. The Lucid key and FloraBase, as search results quote them (the pages themselves were not read), give the ovary half-inferior and usually 2-locular.

traits.woodiness.note: Hutchinson (vol. 1, 2nd ed., 1959), family 164 Rhizophoraceae: trees or shrubs, often on sea shores, with branches swollen at the nodes; leaves opposite with stipules between the leaf stalks that soon fall, rarely alternate and without stipules; leathery, simple.
